groups.rationale: Merges ADR-0237 Windows custodian same-boot recovery (guest-native vscode-web-broker: per-boot custodian generations, generation-scoped job/pipe/version-2 receipts, logon-session quiescence before retiring a prior receipt; windows-editor-v1 stays unselected, native execution pending) with the already-pushed Android display firewall, editor broker readiness and FreeBSD wrong-CID fault-kernel evidence. No catch-all source changed; shared chapters 17, 21 and 22 changed only for ADR-0237, which adds no Ash domain, host, service or deployment placement.

No Marshall source changed; only shared chapters 07, 19 and 20 and the scenario ledger changed for the ADR-0243 native durability scenario (interrupted growth, dm-log-writes power-cut replay, two-host relocation), which claims no Marshall orchestration.
No protocol source changed; shared chapters 07, 19 and 20 changed only to record ADR-0243 native durability evidence, which adds no codec, admission identity or capability.

No Lilly source changed; chapters 07, 19 and 20 record ADR-0243 tests that reuse Lilly Writeback/Sync drive mode as a fixture and explicitly exclude Lilly dataset transfer and relocation orchestration.

Lyra native flush now issues DIOCGFLUSH through gpt/swapfs after UFSRESUME and refuses the receipt on failure (ADR-0243); chapter 07 documents the FreeBSD device cache flush and chapter 20 the power-loss security boundary, refusal and remaining gaps.

New native-durability machine tests and six catalog checks (FreeBSD candidate, promoted omniosGuest), dm-log-writes replay and strace growth-kill tooling, plus the DIOCGFLUSH ABI assertion; chapters 07, 19 and 20 describe the scenarios, recorded passes, the pre-fix FreeBSD failure and gaps. No option or topology change.

ADR-0243, its index and overview entries, the ADR-0190 evidence paragraph and the guest OS matrix review section record native durability method, receipts and gaps; chapters 19 and 20 carry the new scenario and security text.
